name: Friedel-Crafts acylation
notes: Acylium substitution gives an aryl ketone without carbocation rearrangement.

name: Friedel-Crafts alkylation
outcome: Typically 40-80%; rearrangement and polyalkylation can lower selectivity.
notes: Carbocation rearrangement and polyalkylation may occur; strongly deactivated rings do not react.

name: Electrophilic aromatic nitration
outcome: Typically 60-95%; regioselectivity follows substituent directing effects.
notes: The nitronium ion substitutes an aromatic hydrogen; substituents control regioselectivity.

name: Electrophilic aromatic bromination
outcome: Typically 70-95%; ring substitution follows directing effects.
notes: Lewis-acid activation of bromine enables electrophilic aromatic substitution.

name: Electrophilic aromatic chlorination
outcome: Typically 60-90%; ring substitution follows directing effects.
notes: The ring undergoes electrophilic chlorination with regiochemistry set by existing substituents.

name: Electrophilic aromatic sulfonation
notes: Sulfonation is reversible; hot dilute acid can remove the sulfonic acid group.

name: Gattermann-Koch formylation
outcome: Typically 40-75%; installs an aromatic aldehyde group.
notes: Introduces a formyl group onto activated aromatic rings.

name: Electrophilic aromatic iodination
outcome: Typically 50-85%; aryl iodide with substituent-controlled regiochemistry.
notes: An oxidant removes iodide and drives the otherwise reversible electrophilic substitution.

name: Diazotization of aniline
outcome: Typically high conversion to an arenediazonium salt used in situ.
notes: Keep arenediazonium salts cold and dilute; many isolated dry salts are shock-sensitive.

name: Sandmeyer chlorination
outcome: Typically 50-85%; aryl chloride with loss of nitrogen.
notes: Copper(I) chloride replaces the diazonium group; the salt is normally generated and consumed without isolation.

name: Sandmeyer cyanation
outcome: Typically 45-80%; aryl nitrile with loss of nitrogen.
notes: Cyanide handling and acidic diazonium conditions require strict segregation and ventilation.

name: Kolbe-Schmitt carboxylation
outcome: Typically 50-80%; mainly ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid after workup.
notes: Regioselectivity depends on counterion, temperature and pressure; sodium phenoxide commonly favors salicylate.

name: Reimer-Tiemann formylation
notes: Dichlorocarbene-derived formylation is most useful on phenols and can give para isomer as a minor product.
